static_traits.name: Zhu Liya
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive spouse and close friends
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history; no similar psychological problems appeared before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-reflect, good cooperation; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Because of missing the game-winning shot in last week's basketball game, feels disappointed and self-blaming, believes this mistake 'ruined an otherwise good experience', and continually replays the scene and blames themselves.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize I cannot shake off feelings of disappointment and self-blame on my own, which affects my mood and interactions with others, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: Must succeed at critical moments, otherwise I have no value / will disappoint others

special_situations.event: Missing the last-second shot in last week's basketball game, the team failing to win
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I did not make the shot at the critical moment, it proves I am a failure and I have disappointed everyone
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays the mistake in her mind, engages in self-criticism, reduces talking about competitions or participating in related situations to avoid being evaluated again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined this game/I let everyone down

special_situations.event: In work or daily life, recalls basketball-related things or game scenes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the last shot did not go in, then all previous good performance does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distracts attention through work and accompanying family, but inside still continuously focuses on negative fragments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My previous assists and clutch shots are meaningless

special_situations.event: Thinking about the match after interacting or gathering with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I mess up at the critical moment, friends will look down on me or be disappointed in me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Speculates about others' opinions; reduces talking with friends about competitions to avoid embarrassment or evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; actually they think I messed up

special_situations.event: Reviewing the whole match and self-evaluating
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If we did not win at the last moment, I am equivalent to total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Measures performance by extreme standards, binds the result entirely to self-worth

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted by friends and the team, proving his worth at critical moments
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing others, being judged and rejected, worrying self-worth will be negated
defense_goal: Avoids making mistakes again through self-criticism and high standards, reduces talking about competitions to maintain interpersonal safety

object_relations.object_representation: Others are implicit critics / judges (even if supportive on the surface)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites one to review positive performances or resources in matches
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes emphasizing the positive is ignoring 'the fact of failing at critical moments', thus insisting on negative conclusions
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keep a gentle and empathetic tone; use open-ended questions with concretization and emotion naming, guiding connection to present feelings rather than staying at abstract conclusions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about friends' comfort and no longer mentioning the game
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing their own hard-to-accept self-blame to others, believing the others are actually disappointed but only being polite
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In an inquiring tone, gently focuses on evidence and differences in experience, inviting them to distinguish 'speculation' from 'observable signs', avoiding confrontation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When directly facing the self-evaluation 'I am just a failure'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning anger and disappointment about external outcomes against the self, reinforcing self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a steady, low-stimulation tone; use gentle boundaries and reframing, encouraging identifying self-attack patterns and trying more neutral self-descriptions.

manifestations: Viewing the whole game's positive contributions as 'meaningless' because the last shot missed
Negating the value of the process and experience based on the outcome (whether the last shot won the game)

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When talking about the game, shifts attention from positive performance to the final mistake
Uses 'people only remember the last moment' to avoid engaging with the overall experience

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing friends are 'just being polite', attributing one's own disappointment in oneself to others' disappointment in oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Continually blames oneself, demanding of oneself with high standards at critical moments
Ties self-worth entirely to a single result

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling games or interacting with friends, the client usually repeatedly blames oneself and dwells on mistake scenes, leading to low mood and interpersonal tension.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At several gatherings with friends, friends did not yet bring up the game, and the client could continue participating in social interactions, maintaining relationships without on-the-spot conflict yet.
exception_events.reason: Different support and context: friends' actual behavior (keeping invitations going, not mentioning the game) provided cues of acceptance, making it easier to shift attention to interaction rather than rumination in gathering contexts.

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse and friends
Usually coped well with stressful situations in the past
Able to identify and express one's own feelings and needs
Willing to seek professional help and try new methods
negative_force: Strong self-criticism and completely binding self-worth to outcomes
Tending toward mental filtering and negating the positive
Mind reading and personalization tendencies, focuses excessively on others' possible negative evaluations
Persistent worsening rumination and low mood affecting work and interests

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly replays the scene of missing the game-winning shot in the match and engages in self-blame (rumination)
antecedent: Thinking of matches or seeing basketball-related cues
Recalling when alone after interacting with friends
Thinking about the match when distracted at work
target_behavior.core_reason: Uses all-or-nothing standards to equate a single critical mistake with overall failure, binds self-worth to outcomes, and is highly sensitive to others' expectations.
target_behavior.function: Trying to prevent future mistakes through self-criticism and rumination, maintaining control over others' approval (avoiding being judged), while briefly avoiding directly facing shame and disappointment.
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, work performance affected, interpersonal tension, decreased motivation for interests and activities
